output: A Russian SU-27 fighter jet aggressively approached a US RC-135U intelligence-gathering plane in international airspace over the Sea of Okhotsk, manoeuvring to demonstrate it was armed with air-to-air missiles.

Prince Charles and Camilla will embark on a 12-day tour of Australia and New Zealand, visiting various towns and cities, including meeting Malcolm Turnbull, the new Australian PM, between November 10 and 15.
A man is being questioned at Killarney Garda station in connection with a September attack on a woman in Sneem, County Kerry.
Former GP Hugh McGoldrick's name will be erased from the medical register after the Medical Practitioners Tribunal ruling was upheld due to his failure to appeal.
Surrey Police has been given more time to question a 21-year-old male arrested on suspicion of murder, after a man's body was discovered in a wooded area near the Goodwyns housing estate in Dorking.

A 21-year-old man, Josh Hanson, was fatally stabbed shortly after 01:10 BST at the RE bar in Eastcote, Hillingdon, London, and police are urging around 40 potential witnesses who were present at the time to come forward with information.

Hovertravel, a cross-Solent ferry operator, is considering adding a cross-Solent service between Sandown and Southsea, provisionally planned to operate on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 14 July to 27 August.
A 30-year-old man was arrested but released on bail after a victim was attacked by up to eight men in the Heights area at about 02:00 BST on Sunday.

Floods in India have doubled the death toll over the last two days as officials found more than 100 bodies, affecting approximately 450,000 people, prompting government aid and a visit from Prime Minister Narendra Modi to find a "permanent solution" to the recurring flooding.
Arsenal will host Leicester City on the opening night of the 25th anniversary Premier League season on Friday, August 11, at 19:45 BST, with the match airing on Sky Sports.
Oldham Athletic Football Club dismissed Cristian Montano, a player who had been suspended without pay, after he was arrested as part of an investigation into spot-fixing.
A 20-year-old man was given a suspended jail term and supervision order after admitting to starting a fire that destroyed the 42-acre Pontins resort in Brixham in 2014.
Wilson, a 30-year-old, has been without a team since being released in May, having made 51 appearances in his second spell at Forest.
Sri Lanka's slow left-armer Amila Aponso finished with 4-18 to help bowl out Australia for 206, securing a win by 82 runs and leveling the five-match series at 1-1.
Sale Sharks' forward Vadim Cobilas is moving to Bordeaux in France's Top 14, after becoming the first Moldovan international to play in the Premiership.
India's collapse from 277-1 to 323 all out, led by Kane Richardson's 5-68, ended their hopes of a successful run-chase in Australia, as the home side had already sealed the five-match series.

The Hammersmith and City Line has been suspended between Edgware Road and Hammersmith, and part of the Circle Line has been closed, due to the London Fire Brigade's request to mitigate the risk of debris falling onto the tracks following a fire at a 24-storey block.
Jamie Hamill has signed a contract with Kilmarnock, returning to the club where he will make his 150th appearance after previously playing for them.

During an Ipswich v Norwich match, a super-fan accidentally punched a hole in his ceiling while celebrating a goal with a "fist pump" and was later offered repair assistance by the goal-scorer, Paul Anderson.
In Wales, a new law requires retailers to keep cigarettes out of public view unless customers ask for them, with shop managers and assistants facing fines of up to Â£5,000 if they fail to comply.

Lucas, a player who made his debut at Bristol Rovers in 2014, has scored three goals in 10 appearances, and his manager, Luke Garrard, considers him a valuable addition who will provide options in the forward areas.

Network Rail is undertaking maintenance work at Knaresborough station in North Yorkshire, including repairs to the station's watertightness, removal and rebuilding of the signal box's chimney stack, and night-time work on the platform canopy, while Paul Barnfield describes the station as "beautiful" and "steeped in history".

Lawrence Phillips, a former NFL player, was believed to have taken his own life at the age of 40 while serving a prison sentence for assault convictions, including one for driving his car into a group of teenagers and another for assaulting a former girlfriend.

The Belfast Rapid Transit (BRT) plan proposes extending bus lane priorities from 07:00 to 19:00, with potential flexibility through consultation with commuters, stakeholders, and the community along the route.
Lionel Messi grabbed the winner for Barcelona, extending his lead as La Liga's all-time top scorer with his 287th goal in the competition.

Italian authorities have arrested and are investigating over 70 people, including club officials and players, in a match-fixing inquiry led by prosecutors in Catanzaro, with some suspected of links to the 'Ndrangheta crime syndicate.

Approximately 1,600 hybrid spiderlings, bred between species found in Sussex and Suffolk and led by Dr Helen Smith, have been released into suitable dykes at Castle Marshes to give the new population the best potential to adapt to its surroundings and cope with climate change.
The Partition of India in 1947 led to the independence of India from British rule, resulting in millions of people becoming refugees.
Iva Barr, a 20th-time London Marathon participant, tackled the first 14 miles before taking the Underground and walking the remaining distance to the finish line.
In China's top cities, couples are undergoing fake divorces, and young workers face unaffordable housing prices despite low wages.

A 46-year-old landlord, Mr Jones, died at The Blossoms public house in Holyhead on Friday afternoon, and a 24-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder following a stand-off with police on the roof of a neighbouring pub.
This message appears to be a call to action from the BBC, encouraging readers to follow them on social media and share story suggestions.

A fatal car collision occurred on the A713 near Carsphairn, Scotland, where a red Ford Fiesta and a white Asda delivery van collided, resulting in the deaths of two drivers, Antony Sztuka and Scott Kennedy, with the road later re-opening after the incident, and Police Scotland seeking information from the driver of a white flat-bed pickup truck that was in the area at the time of the crash.

Australian rower Sarah Tait, who won an Olympic silver medal in 2012 alongside Kate Hornsey, was remembered as an inspiration and role model after being diagnosed with cervical cancer in 2013, serving as a strong role model to young athletes.

A day after Afghan and US officials signed a deal allowing US troops to stay in Afghanistan, a suicide bomber hit a bus in western Kabul, largely destroying it and injuring two soldiers and two civilians, while the Taliban claimed responsibility for the attack and another in northeast Kabul that killed at least 15 people.
Daimler predicted its full-year sales would be "significantly more than 100bn euros" and reported a 6% increase in sales of 527,600 cars and commercial vehicles in the second quarter.

The 10-year-old son of Crown Prince Frederik of Denmark was saved by a lifeguard from a rip current at Mermaid Beach on the popular Gold Coast strip, with Danish officials later playing down the incident.
A fire occurred in Elgin Road at its junction with Inchbroom Road, where the body of an elderly man was found, with police indicating no suspicious circumstances after their initial inquiries.

Veterans with amputation-related medical issues can now access specialized treatment at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre at Headley Court near Epsom, with six patients already receiving treatment there.

Around 125 drivers per day were caught by new speed cameras on a two-mile stretch of the M4 in Port Talbot, Wales, in the initial period of operation, a decrease from the 700 drivers caught daily during a pilot period.

A Manchester-born teacher, arrested in Valladolid, Spain, is suspected of secretly taking photographs of his students and possessing sexually explicit files involving minors, which were found on his electronic devices.
A seven-year-old sturgeon named Steve, who escaped from World of Water in Romsey, Hampshire during floods, has been found in a deep puddle a mile from the centre, three weeks after going missing.
Chris Rock, a comedian and actor, has filed for divorce from his wife of 19 years, Malaak Compton-Rock, as they work through the process and focus on their two children together.
A collision on the motorway at Tamnamore has caused a closure of both directions, prompting police to advise motorists to exit at specific junctions.

The French government's nomination of diplomat Laurent Stefanini as the new ambassador to the Vatican has been met with silence from the Vatican, which is within the normal six-week response timeframe for such appointments.

The Nasdaq composite index shed 2.4%, or 118 points, to close at 4,876, its biggest one-day drop since April 10 last year, due to declines in semiconductor and biotech stocks, despite Kraft Foods shares soaring more than 35% after a merger announcement.
Czech tennis player Marketa Vondrousova and Croatia's Borna Coric won their respective matches, with Vondrousova edging Kontaveit and Coric saving five match points to defeat Philipp Kohlschreiber.
Stoke City has signed Eric Choupo-Moting, a Cameroonian player who has played as a forward, as one of their summer signings, ahead of their Premier League season opener with a trip to Everton.

Seamus McCollum, a 56-year-old man with cerebral palsy, died at a private nursing home in Randalstown in September, with the death initially not treated as murder until an autopsy in April led to further investigation.

Heavy rains triggered by a depression in the Bay of Bengal have caused widespread flooding and disruptions in India's Tamil Nadu state and Sri Lanka, with around 10,000 people evacuated from their homes in Chennai and the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu announcing a 5bn-rupee relief fund for flood-affected areas.
A McGill's bus caught fire on the A760 Kilbirnie Road outside Largs on Saturday, and despite the incident, the driver and passengers were uninjured.
Notts' Jake Ball is in excellent form, taking six wickets in each of Notts' first two games and being praised by his coaches for his impressive performances with the new ball.

A memorial stone, made from Jersey granite, was unveiled in the French village of Guillemont by Bailiff William Bailhache, with a core of the stone being returned to Jersey to become part of a monument.
A 24-year-old character who played stormtrooper Finn in Star Wars: The Force Awakens visited his childhood theatre company Theatre Peckham to support its young members.
Thailand's Aphibarnrat leads England's Fitzpatrick by one shot at 12 under, with Luke Donald and 15 other players within five strokes of the lead after the second round.
Middlesex ended the day in a strong position, with Simon Voges unbeaten on 128, as the visitors struggled to salvage a draw despite a poor weather forecast for Tuesday.
A 52-year-old woman died and a 16-year-old boy was hospitalized following an incident in Penilee Road, after a 54-year-old man, previously wanted by police, was located in Dumfries and Galloway.

A three-bedroom house in Wavertree, where a young member of The Beatles lived from birth until the age of five, sold at auction to an anonymous telephone bidder for an undisclosed price between £150,000 and £250,000.
Aaron Joseph, 29, has been released on bail and will face trial on February 5 for allegedly owning a dog that was dangerously out of control, after a man was attacked and later died.
A body found on private land near Leighton, about 10 miles from Shrewsbury, is confirmed to be that of Thomas Bebbington, 22, who was last seen entering a river near Shrewsbury on November 10.
Five-week-old baby otters are doing well but still require six feeds each day, and are expected to be fed live food in a future enclosure, which they may be moved to in the summer.

Police in Newtownards are seeking witnesses to a bonfire disturbance on Monday and any activity around the home of Joanne Thompson, a 33-year-old mother-of-four, on Tuesday night and the early hours of Wednesday morning.

This spring, a record 2,270 black-tailed godwits were spotted on the island of Tiree, particularly in a tiny field in Kilmoluaig, where many of the birds, including some from France, Portugal, and Spain, stopped to refuel before their migration to Iceland, often due to adverse northerly winds.
Rangers manager Mark Warburton will not retain first-team coach David Durrant for the start of pre-season training, after Durrant spent 14 years as a player and several years as a coach at the club.
A rare albino deer has been spotted, with biologists estimating that such a birth is unusually rare, occurring once every 100,000 births.

Asad Khan died three weeks after starting at Beckfoot Upper Heaton School in the city of Bradford, with his family claiming he had been bullied and that he had previously expressed feelings of being "unsafe" in school.

A 17th-century painting depicting the 1654 coronation ceremony, which has been hanging in Rokeby Park since at least 1880, is now being investigated by experts to determine its origins and where it came from, after being restored.

Macclesfield Town secured a 3-0 victory over Wrexham, with goals from Danny Rowe, Mitch Hancox, and Danny Whittaker scored in the second half, as the final score reflected a 0-0 start to the second half.

French oil and gas company Total has partnered with the Confederation of African Football (Caf) as the new headline sponsor of its 10 competitions, replacing Orange, in a deal that will begin with the 2017 Africa Cup of Nations finals in Gabon.

Spain's coach Julen Lopetegui has named a squad for the country's first World Cup qualifier, recalling players such as Diego Costa and Juan Mata after they were left out, with Costa and Mata also having been left out of the Euro 2016 squad.

A wildfire, believed to have been started deliberately, has spread across a 5-kilometre area, with 45 firefighters and eight appliances responding to the scene, amidst a total of 435 reported wildfires since May.

Boyd Rankin has made a comeback to Ireland, citing the country's potential to gain Test status as a major draw, and will be available for Ireland's InterContinental Cup match with Papua New Guinea from 31 January to 3 February and then the ICC World Twenty20 in March.

The Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership, created with the Patient Client Council, aims to give sufferers and their carers an independent voice and improve treatment and care for those affected by rare diseases in Northern Ireland.

Gloucester Cathedral is introducing girl choristers to its choir, established since 1539, with auditions scheduled for 23 April and the goal of finding youngsters from local schools and a range of backgrounds to join its musical worship.
Chelsea winger Pedro, 29, who suffered a concussion in a 3-0 win over a Beijing opponent, is expected to return to training with a protective mask.

Nottinghamshire has appointed James Taylor and David Sales to work with their squads, with Taylor bringing a strong 50-over record and Sales offering technical expertise gained from over 20 years of experience.

A man was charged with two counts of criminal damage, disorderly behaviour, and assault on police after an incident on Whiterock Road on Friday afternoon at 15:00 GMT, where children were present, and is due to appear at Belfast Magistrates Court on 5 December.
A volunteer crew from the Larne RNLI launched two lifeboats to assist a yacht whose engine failed a mile north east of Muck Island, towing it to Carrick Marina.
Ipswich Town secured a win over MK Dons, with goals from McGoldrick, Pitman, and Varney, as the teams' managers reflected on the season and the future.

A man from Darlington has been issued with a summons to appear before Maidstone magistrates on 17 February to face charges of dangerous driving, causing serious injury by dangerous driving, and three counts of criminal damage, following a motorway bridge collapse on Saturday 27 August that injured a motorcyclist near the junction with the M26, between junctions four and three, with no fatalities.
A flashmob in Platja d'Aro, Spain, involving several Germans, caused a stampede when bystanders mistook selfie sticks for weapons, resulting in 11 people being treated for injuries.

A two-and-a-half-year-old boy, Jeremiah Regis, was found with over 100 injuries, including a bite to the chest, and later died from abdominal peritonitis caused by blunt force trauma, leading to the charging of his mother and stepfather with murder.
A large gorse fire on Woodbury Common, fanned by high winds, has engulfed a large area of dry heath-land, prompting a multi-crew response, evacuations, and ongoing firefighting efforts overnight.

An agreement has been reached to keep Leicester Speedway going, with a 15-year lease secured for the team's venue, as announced by an unnamed source and confirmed by British Speedway Promoters' Association chairman Keith Chapman.

Elizabeth Bowe, a 50-year-old woman, died three days after being taken to Ninewells Hospital in Dundee following her discovery badly injured in Bobby Jones Place in St Andrews, Scotland, and her brother, Charles Gordon, 51, appeared at Dundee Sheriff Court facing a single charge of murder.
Ross County has signed midfielder Jim O'Brien on a two-year contract after he spent six months on loan with the club, making 18 appearances and scoring twice.
Northants' seam attack exposed Durham's fragile batting line-up, dismissing them for 106 in 45.2 overs, before losing four wickets to finish at 59-3.
The New Zealander is one shot behind joint leaders Brooke Henderson and Lee Mi-rim at the halfway stage of the second women's major.
Gordon Watson will work alongside Mark McGhee as assistant to Scotland manager Gordon Strachan.
The Belfast Giants are in control after the second period, with a 4-1 lead, following goals from Ryan Martinelli and Mark Garside, before Alex Foster increased their advantage.
Spieth's quadruple-bogey collapse at the Masters led to Danny Willett's win, making Willett the first Englishman to win the tournament since Faldo in 1996.

An optometrist, Honey Rose, is on trial for gross negligence manslaughter, accused of allegedly failing to detect a condition during a routine eye test that led to the death of a patient, Vinnie Barker, in a period following his July 2012 eye test at Boots in Ipswich.
China's food price inflation rose to 4.9% in June, a figure below the government's 3.5% target, which may reduce the likelihood of interest rate cuts.

Ivory Coast international Cheick Tiote, who was 30 and played for Newcastle United, died after collapsing during training with the Chinese second-tier side Beijing Enterprises on June 5, with friends, family, and former teammates attending a memorial where his coffin was draped with an Ivory Coast flag.
Slovak rider Peter Sagan won the fifth stage of the race, an uphill sprint, with French rider Thibaut Pinot moving up to second overall in the overall standings.

Cuadrilla's plans for fracking at its Preston New Road site in Lancashire were approved, with the firm promising to put Lancashire "first" for creating jobs, new skills, investment, and community initiatives, but also noting that not all of its expected £50m expenditure in the exploration phase would be spent in the area.

Three 17- and 19-year-old males from north-west London, who were suspected of planning to travel to Syria, were arrested on their return to the UK after being stopped by Turkish officials and later released without charge after further inquiries.

A respiratory consultant at the Royal Berkshire Hospital questioned the £2,500 quote for a blackout blind, suggesting the price may have been excessive, and the hospital stated that the quote was reviewed and 'firmly rejected'.
The young Swans celebrated 31 wins across all competitions in 2016-17 after the cup final.

Denbighshire councillors are considering creating a secondary dune system to strengthen the defences at Barkby Beach in Prestatyn, following severe storms in December that caused damage to an existing dune system.

South Shields will host a tie on 19 August, with commentary by Conor McNamara and Danny Webber, and a game from every stage of the 2017-18 tournament will be streamed live on BBC Sport's digital platforms.
Police Scotland are investigating a targeted attack on a property on Craigmillar Castle Road, where a 38-year-old man suffered serious facial injuries and a second victim, aged 49, was involved.
Pamela McLaggan, 51, was found guilty of manslaughter after Jonathan Baines, 44, was found dead at a house in Gainsborough, and was remanded in custody ahead of sentencing on 21 December.

A 15-year-old boy was assaulted by a man and woman in their 40s at Patterton station on October 3, suffering facial injuries, after an altercation with a group of older people at the station, and his mobile phone was stolen.

Two 17-year-old boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, are feared to have travelled to Syria to join Islamic State in March, having been questioned under section 5 of the Terrorism Act in April and later bailed.
The Great Britain ice hockey team has named a 22-man squad, including three Belfast Giants players, for the Olympic qualifying tournament against Italy, Netherlands, and Serbia in February.
Matthew Perry may appear in a tribute to James Burrows, the creator of Friends, alongside former co-stars, but the tribute is not the reunion fans have been hoping for.

Jones, a 31-year-old footballer, made 41 league appearances for title-winning Championship side Burnley last season, starting their Premier League defeat by Swansea, and has played for Manchester United, Preston, Derby, Blackburn, Wolves, Oldham, and Burnley throughout his career.
Joe Acquaro, a lawyer known in Melbourne's Italian community, was shot dead in the city, with investigators suspecting that underworld bosses may have put a price on his head.

Air France flight AF374 from Paris to Vancouver was diverted to Prestwick due to a slight smell of burning on board, where it landed normally and a second aircraft was sent to fly the passengers back to Charles de Gaulle Airport.

A yellow severe weather warning has been issued for the UK as the remains of Hurricane Gonzalo are expected to bring strong winds and heavy rain, particularly affecting coastal areas and north-western parts of Wales, with gusts exceeding 55mph and the potential for travel disruption.
Children who require urgent medical attention may face prolonged waiting times before being seen by a doctor, due to hospitals being overcrowded.

A 64-year-old man, Kenneth David Dickie, died from his injuries on May 7 at Southampton General Hospital, after which a 34-year-old man was charged with causing grievous bodily harm and a 57-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm with intent and perverting the course of justice.

Nottingham Forest has signed a 24-year-old former Manchester United forward, Filippo Macheda, on loan until the end of the season, with the caveat that he has not started a Championship match this season.
The body of Christopher Huxtable, a 34-year-old man from Swansea, was finally found at the site of a collapsed building.
Bristol City head coach Lee Johnson emphasizes the importance of beating QPR, stating that a win would cut the gap between them and QPR down to five points.
Luca described his experience in space as "absolutely fantastic" and being "giddy with excitement," having orbited Earth 2,656 times during his 2013 mission to the International Space Station.
Hull FC has signed England Knights player Joe Arundel, who made 44 first-team appearances for the Tigers, in a move aimed at building a culture and winning mentality at the club.

Ulster Bank, part of the RBS group, is working to resolve a payment issue affecting approximately 600,000 customers, with the underlying problem now identified and the bank aiming to update payments by Saturday.
Tanzania led Kenya by two goals, with the exact score unspecified, in their 2016 Women's Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, while Ethiopia defeated Uganda 4-1 in a separate play-off match.
McDonald's Japan is rationing French fries due to a shortage caused by industrial action in America, which is affecting 29 ports on the west coast of the United States and impacting potato imports.

The Classic on 3 June will feature a purse of £1.625m, with John Gosden's Cracksman as the favourite, alongside the 1,000-1 outsider Diore Lia, who is running to let her owner generate publicity and funds for Great Ormond Street Children's Hospital.
Atletico Madrid's top scorer Antoine Griezmann will miss France's friendly against Ivory Coast due to a haematoma in his left foot, with an injury to the bone ruled out after an X-ray.
Veteran rugby league player Willie Mason, who has played 290 NRL games and 24 tests for the Kangaroos, was at Manly last season, and is a physical and aggressive player.

A recent survey by The Marine Conservation Society found a 71% increase in dog mess on Scottish beaches and an 11% increase overall in the UK, while dog mess increased overall, overall litter levels were down this year.
The Supreme Court ruled that the government's introduction of fees for employment tribunal cases was unlawful, particularly affecting women, and led to a 79% reduction in such cases.
Wycombe secured a win over Dagenham & Redbridge, moving them up to sixth spot in the league, while Dagenham remain in the relegation places.
Bee-eaters, native to southern Europe, have successfully bred in the UK for a second consecutive summer, with over 1,000 people visiting an RSPB viewpoint at Low Gelt Quarry.
A boy on the bank of the River Wey in Guildford witnessed his father's boat capsize at around 13:10 BST on Monday, and a search is currently underway in the area.

A girl visiting Rabat Zoo in Morocco was fatally injured by a stone thrown by an elephant that was separated from visitors by a fence and a ditch, with experts suggesting the elephant may have been exhibiting frustration.

Labour MP Ms Glass has been appointed to a shadow cabinet role, replacing Ms Powell, who resigned citing Jeremy Corbyn's "untenable" position as Labour party leader, amid a wave of resignations by Labour MPs.
Chelsea manager Conte believes six teams, including Manchester United, among others, can fight to win the title with 14 games remaining.

A dispersal order has been issued in Llangefni, allowing police and community support officers to remove troublemakers and protect young people from anti-social behavior and the effects of excessive drinking.
Middlesbrough manager Garry Monk confirmed the Championship club's interest in signing Chelsea midfielder Lewis Baker, while also mentioning Marten de Roon's performance in the current season.
The Roald Dahl Funny Prize, established in 2008 to recognize humorous children's books, is to be relaunched in 2016 as part of the author's centenary celebrations.

Frazier Glenn Miller Jr, a 74-year-old white supremacist, was convicted of capital murder and other charges, including the killings of two people, after a trial in which he represented himself and expressed a motivation to kill Jews.

The city council plans to launch a self-service bike scheme in April 2017, with 500 bikes located across the city at easily accessed sites, similar to the "Boris bikes" scheme in London, which allows bikes to be hired and returned to any empty docking point.
West Ham's 27-year-old player has returned to light training after back surgery and will need time to reach sufficient fitness levels before being considered for Premier League selection.

Property prices in Northern Ireland rose by up to 5.4% annually in the third quarter, with prices almost flat compared to the second quarter at 0.8%, and the average standardised price reaching just over £124,000.

A recent delivery of a huge wind turbine part on the A713 in Dumfries and Galloway ended up in a ditch, while a separate delivery on Bargrennan Bridge was successfully navigated, highlighting varying outcomes of transporting such large items on country roads.

The Betsi Cadwaladr health board is considering downgrading services at one of the area's three district hospitals due to staffing shortages, but residents are opposing the plan, citing concerns over increased travel for women's care.
South Africa's Mignon du Preez hit a second ODI century (116 off 99 balls) to help her team to a 68-run victory over Ireland.

British high jumper Holly Peake aims to break her own Welsh record and qualify for the Rio Olympics by surpassing the qualification standard of 4.50m, which she has yet to achieve, as her personal best is 4.40m.
A fire at a building site in Bloomery Circle, believed to have been deliberately set, burned for more than 10 hours before being extinguished.

A charity event organized by Mercy Corps, the Nepal Scotland Association, and the city council was held in the city, featuring the City Chambers on the Royal Mile, to raise money for the Nepal earthquake relief effort.

Uefa imposed a punishment on Hibernian head coach Neil Lennon, automatically banning him from the touchline for the return leg of the Europa League qualifying match, following his remonstrations with officials.

A fire started at the ICL UK Boulby mine, 1,100m (3,600 ft) under the sea bed, on April 13, resulting in seven workers being treated for smoke inhalation and prompting a notice from the Health and Safety Executive, with more than 100 staff temporarily unaccounted for, and the company required to comply with the notice by June 27.

Two men, including a 23-year-old British national, were removed from a Unesco World Heritage site after being caught posing naked by surveillance workers, and are reportedly being questioned over minor morality offences.
Croatia international Ivan Rakitic is set to sign a new deal with Barcelona on Friday, which has a £109m buyout clause.

A couple from Halstead suffered life-changing injuries during a two-hour incident on April 26, with police continuing their investigation and releasing a computer-generated image of a black man who may be involved.

The Wickerman Festival, taking place on July 25-26 near Dundrennan, has announced its initial lineup, featuring Dizzee Rascal as the opening night headliner alongside other acts including Martha Reeves and The Vandellas.

Foden expressed hope that his and Saints' strong performance would bring out the best in both him and England, potentially leading to more England players from Saints being selected for the upcoming Six Nations tournament.
A 22-year-old motorcyclist died after a collision with a Vauxhall Zafira car in Dagenham, while a 7-year-old boy remains in serious condition as a rear passenger in the car.

Pfizer has agreed to acquire Anacor Pharmaceuticals, with the goal of addressing a significant unmet medical need, as the company's flagship product, crisaborole, can achieve $2bn in annual sales if approved by the US FDA, addressing a condition affecting 18 million to 25 million people in the US.
Police at Oxlow Lane, Dagenham, recovered knives, scissors, and cannabis from a large and unpredictable crowd involved in a reported street fight, leading to the arrest of two boys, aged 17 and 15.
A 23-year-old man from Cardiff was arrested on suspicion of sexual assault in connection with an incident at Gorsedd Gardens near Cardiff Civic Centre.

Conservative MSP John Lamont has resigned from the Ettrick, Roxburgh and Berwickshire constituency seat to seek to unseat the SNP's Calum Kerr in the nearby Berwickshire, Roxburgh and Selkirk constituency.

The EU has gained access to new markets for its beef exports, with Canada agreeing to accept beef from countries including the UK, Ireland, France, and Germany, and the US also accepting beef from the EU under strict monitoring, following a free trade agreement that the EU is currently in the process of ratifying.

European finance ministers have endorsed plans for a single EU list of "non-cooperative jurisdictions" by the end of the summer, with the European Commission suggesting sanctions for nations that fail to change their tax practices.

Archaeologists monitoring the building of the new West Link road in Inverness, Scotland, have discovered Bronze Age burnt mounds and pottery fragments, which are associated with the ancient use of heated stones for cooking, washing wool, or as small saunas.
Main scored after the hour mark, securing a victory that leaves Oldham with a sizeable cushion above the League One relegation places.
Pierce Lally passed away peacefully in hospital after a short illness, having worked on notable projects such as Glenroe, Ballykissangel, and The Secret of Kells.
Derby City Council has committed to keeping Moorways Pool open for a year after identifying Â£350,000 in annual savings through cuts in back-office areas and management restructuring.

Human rights groups, including those led by Manuel Fontaine of the UN Children's fund (Unicef), are concerned that children detained by the Nigerian army as part of its counter-insurgency operations against Boko Haram may not be following a proper legal process.

Hearts head coach Robbie Neilson may look at signing Lee Hollis, a 28-year-old goalkeeper who became a free agent after leaving Motherwell this summer, as the team assesses its situation after an injury.

Chelsey Lee, a South Korean basketball player, is facing a lifetime suspension and record annulment in the Korean Women's Basketball League after allegations of fabricating her and her father's birth certificates to show she had a South Korean grandmother.

Ofcom's app samples wireless signals to identify potential speed slowdowns and provides tips, released alongside research that highlights progress in UK telecoms services, including improved broadband speeds, but also notes that 2.4 million homes lack speeds of 10Mbps or more.

Manchester United's Paul Pogba and Zlatan Ibrahimovic discussed the impact of social media and pressure on players, with Ibrahimovic stating that top players put pressure on themselves and that he personally prefers team success over individual achievements.

A metal object, later confirmed as a payload shroud from the Alphasat satellite launch, was found in the municipality of Salinopolis and has been confirmed by the UK Space Agency to be from the Alphasat launch, with Brazilian authorities planning to contact the agency to arrange its collection.

Former Culture Secretary James Purnell warned that downgrading TV licence fee evasion to a civil offence would lead to increased non-payment, potentially forcing the government to have a higher licence fee or the loss of services such as BBC Four, CBBC, and CBeebies.
